reviewAssignments.details: Blocking finding F-0001: interrupted task creation may duplicate the task on retry.

findings.summary: Interrupted task creation can create a duplicate
findings.details: A failed or interrupted create can be recovered and then retried as a second task, leaving an unintended duplicate plan entry and returning a different ID. TaskService.ts:31-57 always allocates and writes a new task after entering the transaction. WorkspaceTransaction.ts:37,115-166 first replays any pending ledger write and commits it before the operation runs. Unlike TicketService.ts:43,99-114, task creation does not inspect recovered writes to recognize its already-recovered operation. Existing task tests do not exercise this recovery path. Make an interrupted task-create retry recognize the recovered creation and return its original ID without creating another task. Add an interruption/recovery regression test, while retaining distinct IDs for genuinely separate creates.

findings.summary: Accepted task reports are not revalidated after acceptance
findings.details: TaskService verifies the report digest during acceptance (TaskService.ts:332-342), but ticket submission, integration, and closure gates rely on accepted status without revalidating the report (TaskPlanPolicy.ts:108-115, SubmissionService.ts:114, TicketIntegrationService.ts:211-218, ChecksService.ts:341-345). Mutating or deleting an accepted report therefore does not invalidate acceptance or prevent ticket completion. Preserve the accepted evidence by validating stored digests at completion gates or making evidence immutable, and test both mutation and deletion.

findings.summary: Task assignment can persist when handoff construction fails
findings.details: TaskService marks and persists the task as assigned before handoff() validates the parent ticket sections (TaskService.ts:241-246, 481-500; WorkspaceTransaction.ts:170-197, 232-239). A missing or empty Requirements or Acceptance Criteria section can therefore make the command fail after reserving the task and its write paths, leaving an assignment without a delivered handoff. Build/validate the handoff before persistence or roll back, and test that failure leaves the ledger unchanged.
